clue.text: They are pressed into service to, study texts

parts.note: to con is an old verb meaning to study or learn by heart
scripts are written texts

explanation.surface: Someone goes into service to study written texts.
explanation.definitionFit: Conscripts are people compulsorily enlisted, as if pressed men in the navy of old.

clue.text: Prehistoric European tool

explanation.surface: An archaeologist labels a Stone Age implement.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is an ancient Briton or Gaul; the other is an archaeologist's word for a prehistoric chisel or axe head.

clue.text: Sign up submarine captain

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: an omen is a sign or portent

explanation.surface: A captain enlists to command a submarine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns OMEN round. Captain Nemo commands the submarine Nautilus in Jules Verne's novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Jules Verne's Captain Nemo commands the submarine Nautilus.

clue.text: Intends to cheat models

parts.note: to con someone is to cheat or swindle them
templates are patterns or models to copy

explanation.surface: Someone plans to swindle the fashion models.
explanation.definitionFit: To contemplate doing something is to have it in mind, to plan it.

clue.text: Put in gravel — no end of it!

definitions.text: Put in gravel — no end of it!

parts.words: Put in gravel — no end of it!
parts.note: drop the last letter of gravel and you have put in the grave, which is to bury

explanation.surface: A gardener spreads gravel endlessly over a path.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as one instruction: 'gravel' without its final L is GRAVE, and to put in the grave is to bury a body.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to bury, lay a body in its grave.

clue.text: Palatable, but not quite so hot to me

indicators.note: words that are not quite right are slightly out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone finds a dish tasty but a little too spicy for them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' is the anagram signal: SO HOT TO ME rearranged gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Toothsome food is tasty, pleasant to eat.

clue.text: Eg Don Juan's part in fine picture

indicators.note: the answer is a part sitting inside the words fine picture, across the gap

explanation.surface: Someone says Don Juan plays a role in a good film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part in' signals letters found running across 'finE PICture'. Byron's Don Juan is a long narrative poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Byron's Don Juan is a long narrative poem, an example of the heroic genre.

clue.text: Fussy or laid-back? No original

parts.note: prim means fussily proper

indicators.note: back, hyphened onto laid, tells us to read that word from its end to its start

parts.note: taken as written, before it is turned

explanation.surface: Is someone fussy or relaxed? Neither: they are original.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid-back' reads as 'relaxed', but split it is a word and its reversal signal; 'No' is surface padding before the definition, as if rejecting both options.
explanation.definitionFit: Primordial means existing from the very beginning, first or original.

clue.text: The middleman's position can be learnt in the city

indicators.note: the letters can be rearranged into something else, an anagram signal

explanation.surface: A broker's trade can be learnt in the City of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' signals rearranging LEARNT and CITY together.
explanation.definitionFit: Centrality is the state of being in the middle, the place a go-between occupies.

clue.text: Platelayer's function

parts.note: not a railway track worker but something that lays down thin plates or sheets one on another

explanation.surface: What does a railway track worker do?
explanation.walkthrough: A platelayer is a British railway worker who lays and maintains track; here it means one who layers plates.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamination is building something up from thin sheets bonded in layers.

clue.text: Auditor's shabby appearance

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: mean can mean shabby or squalid

explanation.surface: An accountant looks rather scruffy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' looks like an accountant but means a hearer, the homophone signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's mien is their bearing or look.

clue.text: Image-building 'in church by memorial to royal exhibitionist

definitions.text: Image-building 'in church by memorial to royal exhibitionist

parts.words: Image-building 'in church by memorial to royal exhibitionist
parts.note: the royal consort who organised the Great Exhibition of 1851, commemorated by a statue in a church-like Gothic memorial

explanation.surface: A statue stands in a Gothic shrine honouring a royal showman.
explanation.walkthrough: The Albert Memorial in London's Kensington Gardens is a Gothic, church-like canopy over a statue of Queen Victoria's consort, who championed the Great Exhibition of 1851.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen Victoria's consort promoted the Great Exhibition, so he was literally the royal exhibitionist.

clue.text: On the quiet, nobleman takes shelter in Hawaii

definitions.text: On the quiet, nobleman takes shelter in Hawaii

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet
an earl is a British nobleman
a harbour is a shelter for ships

explanation.surface: A peer quietly finds refuge on a Pacific island.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the place: a sheltered anchorage in Hawaii, the US naval base attacked in 1941.
explanation.definitionFit: The US naval base on Oahu is a sheltered anchorage in the Hawaiian islands.

clue.text: Work-to win result

parts.note: to take a prize is to win it
an effect is a result

explanation.surface: Someone works hard to win a good outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: A medicine or law that starts to operate is said to work.

clue.text: How one may go off the point when attending a function

definitions.text: How one may go off the point

parts.note: to be at an event is to attend it
the tangent is a trigonometric function

explanation.surface: A guest at a dinner drifts off the subject of conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'function' suggests a social event, but it is the maths function; a tangent also touches a curve at one point and then goes off.
explanation.definitionFit: To fly off at a tangent is to digress suddenly from the subject.

clue.text: As a starter Herod returns holy books

parts.note: Herod Antipas was the ruler of Galilee in the Gospels

indicators.note: returns means the letters come back, read in reverse

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of holy books

explanation.surface: Herod opens proceedings by giving back the scriptures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns OT into TO.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian hors d'oeuvre served before the main meal.

clue.text: Navicular trig!

explanation.surface: A puzzled student reads out two odd technical words.
explanation.definitionFit: Navicular means boat-shaped, a vessel's form; trig is an old word for neat and trim, like a tidy vessel.

clue.text: Donald endlessly confused about a knotty point

indicators.note: confused letters are jumbled into a new order
without its end, so the last letter of Donald is removed

explanation.surface: Donald is baffled by a tricky problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts Donald to DONAL; 'confused' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodal means relating to a node, a knot or knob-like point.

clue.text: One of the crowd takes cover in the field

explanation.surface: A spectator ducks for shelter on the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, extra cover is a fielding position, so the word joins cover to name a place in the field.
explanation.definitionFit: A film extra is a member of a crowd scene; extra cover is a cricket fielding place.

clue.text: Get inn ale analysed: it's of crude type

indicators.note: analysed means broken down into parts, so these letters are taken apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: A drinker is told to have the pub's beer tested because it is rough stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'analysed' rearranges GET INN ALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Inelegant means lacking grace, clumsy or coarse.

clue.text: Those of the billiards sharp were to be fitless, said Gilbert

definitions.text: Those of the billiards sharp were to be fitless, said Gilbert

parts.words: Those of the billiards sharp were to be fitless, said Gilbert
parts.note: in The Mikado the cheating billiards player is punished by playing in ill-fitting finger coverings

explanation.surface: A quotation from Gilbert and Sullivan about a cheating billiards player.
explanation.walkthrough: In W S Gilbert's Mikado song 'A more humane Mikado', the billiard sharp must play 'in fitless finger-stalls, on a cloth untrue, with a twisted cue'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheaths worn over a finger, which in Gilbert's lyric the cheat must wear badly fitted.

clue.text: He sounds a bore, this soothsayer

indicators.note: sounds says the word is spoken, a homophone

parts.note: an auger is a tool for boring holes

explanation.surface: A fortune-teller is said to be tedious company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bore' looks like a dull person but is a boring tool, the auger.
explanation.definitionFit: An augur was a Roman priest who foretold events from omens.

clue.text: Christian.X taken in by doctor — designing fellow!

indicators.note: one piece is taken inside another, a container signal

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral ten, written 10 and read as the letters IO

explanation.surface: King Christian X is fooled by a scheming physician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Christian' points to the designer's first name, Christian Dior, and also suggests the Danish king Christian X; X is 10, read as IO.
explanation.definitionFit: Christian Dior was the French fashion designer behind the New Look.

clue.text: Lines up under ambassador — simple!

indicators.note: in a down clue, the lines come under the ambassador, so after him

parts.note: HE is His Excellency, an ambassador's title

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: BR stands for British Rail, railway lines

explanation.surface: An envoy lines up subordinates for an easy task.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns BR into RB. 'simple' is a noun here: an old word for a medicinal plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple is an old name for a medicinal plant, one used on its own.

clue.text: Watchers get down to bingo as instructed

definitions.text: get down to bingo as instructed

explanation.surface: Players settle down to a bingo game when told to.
explanation.walkthrough: The bingo caller's opening cry is 'Eyes down!', telling players to look at their cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyes are the organs that watch; at bingo the instruction to start play is to put them down.

clue.text: Flower for the Queen of Navarre

explanation.surface: A bloom is chosen for a French queen.
explanation.definitionFit: The ox-eye daisy bears this name, as did the sixteenth-century writer queen Marguerite de Navarre.

clue.text: The Marshal jumped to it

indicators.note: letters that have jumped about are mixed up into a new order

explanation.surface: A soldier springs into action on the Marshal's command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumped' rearranges TO IT. Marshal Tito led Yugoslavia.
explanation.definitionFit: Josip Broz, Yugoslavia's leader, held the rank of Marshal.

clue.text: Crush pulse

explanation.surface: A teenager's infatuation makes the heart race.
explanation.definitionFit: A crush is a person one is infatuated with, an idol; a pulse is a beat of the heart.
